questions.enonce_markdown: (a) State two properties of the probability density function of the normal distribution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two of the following properties (a normal density curve $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(x - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}$):

1. **The curve is bell-shaped and symmetrical about the mean** $x = \mu$, so the mean, median and mode are all equal to $\mu$.
2. **The total area under the curve is $1$** (the probabilities of all possible values add up to $1$), and each half of the curve (either side of $\mu$) has area $0.5$.

Other accepted properties: the curve is asymptotic to the $x$-axis (it never touches it) in both directions; it has a single maximum at $x = \mu$; it has points of inflexion at $x = \mu \pm \sigma$; about $68\%$, $95\%$ and $99.7\%$ of the values lie within $1$, $2$ and $3$ standard deviations of the mean.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A random variable $X$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu$, and variance $\sigma^2$. Given that $97.72\%$ of the values of $X$ are below $80$ and $0.14\%$ are above $90$,

(b) find, to the nearest integer, the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, and $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \sim N(0, 1)$ with distribution function $\Phi$.

**First condition.** $P(X < 80) = 0.9772$, so $P\!\left(Z < \dfrac{80 - \mu}{\sigma}\right) = 0.9772$. From the normal tables $\Phi(2.00) = 0.9772$, hence

$$\frac{80 - \mu}{\sigma} = 2.00 \qquad (1)$$

**Second condition.** $P(X > 90) = 0.0014$, so $P\!\left(Z < \dfrac{90 - \mu}{\sigma}\right) = 1 - 0.0014 = 0.9986$. From the tables $\Phi(2.99) = 0.9986$, hence

$$\frac{90 - \mu}{\sigma} = 2.99 \qquad (2)$$

**Solving.** Subtracting (1) from (2): $\dfrac{10}{\sigma} = 0.99$, so $\sigma = 10.10\ldots \approx 10$. Then $\mu = 80 - 2.00\sigma = 80 - 20.2 = 59.8 \approx 60$.

**$\mu = 60$ and $\sigma = 10$** (to the nearest integer). Check: $\dfrac{80 - 60}{10} = 2$ and $\dfrac{90 - 60}{10} = 3$, which give $\Phi(2) = 0.9772$ and $1 - \Phi(3) = 0.0013 \approx 0.0014$.
